correctness.rationale: For every finite nonempty quiver, q a prime power and k≥1, the proof establishes both directions of the diagonal-separation and independent corner-rank criterion. Lifting mutually orthogonal idempotents through B∩J and explicitly conjugating by the 1+J element aligns the diagonal subalgebra; a hyperplane in a deficient corner gives a proper containing subalgebra. Uniform independent map ranks produce the finite product. Positivity gives the exact generator minimum, and logarithmic expansions with explicit remainders give the asymptotic threshold. A separate exact multiplication-closure verifier exhaustively checked 19 configurations over fields with 2, 3 and 4 elements; finite tests are corroboration, not a substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected random-generation paper arXiv:2009.01115 proves general upper/lower bounds and maximal-subalgebra structure, not the exact independent-corner generating-tuple product or the many-vertex fixed-field birthday law. The close structural antecedent arXiv:1705.00762 classifies maximal subalgebras, including those of quiver algebras (Proposition 4.2), but does not enumerate generating tuples. The 2010 study arXiv:1001.2873 treats chiefly semisimple/algebraic-number settings and states that nontrivial-radical generator formulas require further work. An exact general derivation from broader uninspected work remains the principal priority risk.

value.rationale: The result completely determines the natural generator-tuple probability across all radical-square-zero finite quiver algebras, including loops and parallel arrows, and determines the minimum number of algebra generators. It exhibits an unusual orientation/placement invariance and a sharp random-generation threshold near twice the deterministic logarithmic generator scale; edge density changes the critical probability constant. These features are structural and motivated by existing probabilistic generation theory, not arbitrarily selected finite cases.
